column3: “Going and strong … going and weak” is rendered “grew steadily stronger … grew weaker continually.”
“The wife of Nabal” is rendered “the widow of Nabal.”
NASB names “Ish-bosheth” as the speaker; the Hebrew has only “he said.”
“Loyalty” is rendered “kindness,” and “visited on me” as “charge me with.”
NASB supplies “I do not” in the oath (“if … I do not accomplish this”).
Close to the Hebrew; NASB keeps the repeated “saying” as one quotation.
NASB supplies “first,” and “see my face” at the end becomes “see me.”
“The word of Abner was with” is rendered “Abner had consultation with,” and “both yesterday and the third day” as “In times past.”
“Act” is rendered “do it!”; “has spoken to David” is rendered “has spoken of David.”
“In the ears of” is rendered “in the hearing of.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB supplies “they” as those who told.
“He has gone completely” is rendered “he is already gone.”
“Exit and entrance” is rendered “going out and coming in.”
“Let them whirl over” is rendered “May it fall on”; “one with a skin disease” is rendered “a leper,” and “spindle” as “distaff.”
